title: OnSIP alternatives: 10 options to try in 2026
summary: Not sure if OnSIP is the right phone solution for your needs? Compare 10 of the best OnSIP alternatives, plus pricing and features, here.
body_markdown:
Whether you’re a current or a potential OnSIP customer, you might be wondering: “Is this really the right fit for my business?” Between its pay-as-you-go pricing and missing collaboration tools, it’s not a good fit for small and growing businesses.


You’re probably better off with a different solution, but who has the time to go through them all? To save you time, we rounded up the 10 best OnSIP alternatives, including their pros, cons, and potential costs.


In this post, we’ll summarize several of the top options available:


- **Quo:** Best solution for growing teams
- **Dialpad:** Best for international phone numbers
- **Nextiva:** Great for omnichannel communications
- **Ooma:** Ideal for unlimited calling to Mexico and Puerto Rico
- **RingCentral:** Best provider for renting desk phones
- **8×8:** Best alternative for high-volume operations
- **Vonage:** Best platform for video conferencing
- **Grasshopper:** Top option for multi-digit extensions
- **Aircall:** Great alternative if you need power dialers
- **Phone.com:** Best alternative for HIPAA-compliant video calling


Scroll down to find the best OnSIP alternative for you.


##


**Comparing the best OnSIP alternatives**


Here’s a quick overview of the different business phone solutions:

We’ll start with the #1 business phone solution as rated by G2.


### **1. Quo: Best OnSIP alternative for small and growing businesses**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calling and SMS to the US and Canada
- 9,000+ integrations on all plans via Zapier and Make
- Automated texting workflows
- AI agent, Sona
- Internal threads, or team chat


#### Cons


- No verification through two-factor authentication*


**Nearly all virtual phone numbers share this problem. Companies like Facebook, Uber, and Google rarely let you authenticate accounts through a virtual phone number.*


Quo is a next-generation business phone platform for startups and growing businesses. Each plan comes with unlimited calls and texts to the US and Canada, one number per user, and additional numbers if needed.


Quo makes it easy for your team to work together and stay on the same page. You’ll get shared numbers, for example, so multiple team members can collaborate on conversations while maintaining history and context. Need to delegate tasks? Use internal threads to tag team members and collaborate behind the scenes.


Unlike OnSIP, which has limitations on voicemail, Quo’s[voicemail](https://www.quo.com/product/voicemail) comes standard with no limits. We also offer free[voicemail transcription](https://www.quo.com/features/voicemail-to-text) on every plan. That way, your team can keep better records and share information more easily.


Plus, you can avoid missed calls altogether with Sona, Quo’s AI agent. Sona answers calls 24/7, handles common questions, captures key details, and ensures you never miss a customer call again. It’s an always-on receptionist that gets smarter over time so your team can focus on growing your business.


You can also use Quo to save time texting — something that OnSIP can’t help with. You’ll have access to:


- [Scheduled messages](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-schedule-texts)
- Templated texts, also known as snippets
- [Auto-replies](https://www.quo.com/blog/texting-auto-reply-examples/) to missed calls


There are also integrations to third-party tools like Slack, HubSpot, and Salesforce. Quo connects with more than 9,000 apps through Zapier and Make, starting on the base plan. Plus, Quo has direct connectors with tools like Claude and ChatGPT. Quo connects to the tools your team already uses. You can improve your workflow and gain insights into your business by tapping into your third-party tool ecosystem.


More than 90,000 customers rely on Quo to help them answer faster and stay organized.[Sign up for a seven-day free trial](https://my.quo.com/signup) and see why.


#### **Key features of Quo**


- AI call tags
- Local, toll-free, and vanity numbers
- Shared phone numbers
- [Call recording](https://www.quo.com/product/call-recording)
- Voicemail transcripts
- [Call screening](https://www.quo.com/product/call-management/call-screening)
- Automations with Zapier and Make
- [Quo API](https://www.quo.com/api)
- Analytics
- [Phone menus](https://www.quo.com/blog/phone-menu/)


#### **Quo pricing**


[Quo pricing](https://www.quo.com/pricing) is transparent across its three tiers:


- **Starter:** $15 per user per month for unlimited calling and messaging to the US and Canada, voicemail, shared contacts, group messaging, and more
- **Business:** $23 per user per month for group calls, call transfers, Salesforce and HubSpot integrations, and more
- **Scale:** $35 per user per month for AI call tags, inbound phone support, priority support, and dedicated onboarding


### **2. Dialpad: Best for using international phone numbers**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calling to US and Canadian numbers
- Supports numbers from 50+ countries
- Desktop and mobile apps are available


#### Cons


- User minimums on higher-tier plans
- Limit of 250 outbound messages per user per month
- No additional numbers without upgrading
- Unreliable service, according to user reviews


[Dialpad](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-alternatives/) is a virtual phone system established in 2011. It supports international numbers from over 50 countries, which is useful if you’re expanding overseas. If you don’t want an international number, you can purchase a toll-free number instead. This costs $15 per number per month, plus $0.02 per minute for incoming calls.


Their base plan is the most comparable to OnSIP’s on this list. It features unlimited calling within the US and Canada, call recording, and more.


Dialpad is a decent platform if you do most of your business overseas. But if you do more than just *call* customers, it could be limiting and expensive. For example, there’s a 250-message limit on outbound messages. If you go over that, you’ll pay $0.008 per SMS and $0.024 per MMS.


Keep in mind that plans user minimums as you upgrade. Coupled with unreliable service, according to user reviews, you may pay more than is necessary for a quality VoIP platform. See for yourself:


“ *Our business text messages are blocked far too often, making the platform unreliable for customer communication.”* —[Trustpilot](https://www.trustpilot.com/reviews/6a7361151b3b7f097fe63793)


### Key features of Dialpad


**


- Outbound SMS, with limits
- Custom call routing
- Call forwarding
- Team messaging
- Three-way calling


### Dialpad pricing


**


[Dialpad pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/dialpad-pricing/) for its core product has three plans:


- **Standard:** $15 per person per month for calls, outbound SMS, call forwarding, call routing, and voicemail transcriptions
- **Pro:** $25 per person per month for additional numbers, hold queues, and 25[ring groups](https://www.quo.com/features/ring-groups?ps_partner_key=Njk2MjU0NmQwOTVm&ps_xid=rczle723qPVVHH) ; requires a three-seat minimum.
- **Enterprise:** Custom quote for unlimited ring groups, 99.9% uptime, and user access controls


### **3. Nextiva: Best for omnichannel communications**


#### Pros


- Omnichannel communication with calls, texts, social media, live chat, and video
- Inbound and outbound calls in the US and Canada


#### Cons


- SMS and MMS are limited to 100 messages per user per month
- Call recording requires an upgrade
- Toll-free number requires an upgrade
- Most integrations have an add-on fee


[Nextiva](https://www.quo.com/blog/nextiva-alternatives/) is an omnichannel communications platform for talking to customers across multiple channels. A single customer can switch between calls, texting, web chat, and social media DMs. This all shows up in Nextiva’s platform, so you can easily get context from the entire chain of a customer’s conversations.


That said, Nextiva has a relatively low limit for to SMS/MMS messages. You get just 100 messages per user per month on the Core plan. Texting is also only available for local numbers. International messaging isn’t available at all. This could be tricky if you work with overseas customers.


You should also know Nextiva doesn’t offer a trial. This means you won’t be able to try it out before signing up — unlike other OnSIP alternatives, like Quo.


### Key features of Nextiva


**


- Unlimited calls and video meetings
- Team messaging
- Contact management
- Shared inbox
- Desktop, web, and mobile app


### Nextiva pricing


**


Here are the[Nextiva pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/nextiva-pricing/) plans for small businesses:


- **Core:** $15 per user per month for calls and texts to the US and Canada, social media messaging, video calls, and email
- **Engage:** $25 per user per month for free access to toll-free numbers, online fax, call recording, live chat, and integration with Microsoft Teams
- **Scale:** $75 per user per month for real-time call transcriptions, AI call notes and summaries, and unlimited text messages


### **4. Ooma: Best for calling Mexico and Puerto Rico**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calling in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico
- Toll-free number with 500 minutes of inbound calls per month in the US


#### Cons


- Texting requires an upgrade
- Call recording requires an upgrade
- Scheduled messaging requires an upgrade
- No integrations in the base plan


[Ooma](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-alternatives/) is a home and business phone provider. For business owners, it allows for unlimited calling in the US, Canada, Puerto Rico, and Mexico. It also owns OnSIP’s platform. It purchased OnSIP in 2022.


Ooma’s base plan includes a virtual receptionist, free porting, and a local or free toll-free number. You can also unlock certain AI capabilities if you upgrade a few times. For example, you get AI transcriptions and AI insights if you upgrade to the Pro Plus plan at $29.95 per month.


Just know there’s no messaging on Ooma Office’s base plan. It’s also missing other basic features, like call recording, a desktop app, and voicemail transcription.. This might be costly and confusing for small businesses that just need the basics.


### Key features of Ooma Office


**


- Unlimited calling in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico
- E911
- Three-way calling
- Call transfer
- Ring group


### Ooma Office pricing


**


Here’s what to expect from[Ooma pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/ooma-pricing/) :


- **Ooma Office Essentials:** $19.95 per user per month for unlimited calling in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Puerto Rico, free porting, and a free toll-free number with incoming call minutes
- **Ooma Office Pro:** $24.95 per user per month for 100 text messages, calling from the desktop app, and call recording
- **Ooma Office Pro Plus:** $29.95 per user per month for 400 text messages, shared voicemail boxes, call screening, and CRM integrations
- **Ooma Office Enterprise:** Custom quote for Microsoft Teams integration, advanced analytics, and custom implementations


### **5. RingCentral: Best for renting desk phones**


#### Pros


- Desk phone rentals are available on every plan
- Unlimited calls in the US and Canada
- Local and toll-free numbers


#### Cons


- Phone rentals require a multi-year contract
- Call recordings are deleted after 90 days
- Limited toll-free minutes and text messages


[RingCentral](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-alternatives/) is a virtual phone system for business owners who favor a more traditional office setup. You can rent desk phones for physical locations, like your rep’s cubicles. That said, renting phones requires a minimum initial term of 24 months. That’s on top of the headaches of setting up and maintaining additional hardware.


RingCentral’s Core plan includes unlimited calls to the US and Canada. However, you only get 25 text messages per user per month on their base plan. You also get just 100 toll-free minutes, which is barely over 1.5 hours of calls per month.


Other features of their base plan include voicemail transcripts and on-demand call recording. But keep in mind that on-demand call recordings are deleted after 90 days, no matter how many times you choose to upgrade.


### Key features of RingCentral


**


- Free business and toll-free numbers
- Unlimited calling in the US and Canada
- Shared phone numbers
- AI noise cancellation
- Desk and conference phone rentals


### RingCentral pricing


**


There are four[RingEx pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-pricing/) plans to consider:


- **Core:** $20 per user per month for unlimited calls, 100 toll-free minutes, and 25 SMS/MMS per user
- **Advanced:** $25 per user per month for 1,000 pooled toll-free minutes, 100 SMS/MMS per user, automatic call recording, advanced call routing, and integrations with CRMs
- **AI Customer Engagement Bundle with AIR:** 10,000 pooled toll-free minutes, 200 SMS per user, unlimited storage, and historical and real-time insights. Contact sales for pricing
- **AI Customer Engagement Bundle with AIR and ACE:** AI Conversation Expert (ACE), coaching and performance analytics, and CRM and productivity integrations. Contact sales for pricing.


### **6. 8×8: Best for high-volume operations**


#### Pros


- High-volume messaging is available
- International phone numbers
- Unified communications


#### Cons


- Opaque pricing
- Complex features list
- Complicated setup


[8×8](https://www.quo.com/blog/8x8-alternatives/) is a unified communications platform designed for mid- to large contact centers. Features include video meetings, queue management, and omnichannel routing. These are useful if you need to monitor a lot of reps and provide feedback or coaching.


Today, 8×8 organizes its plans by use case, like “Contact Center” and “Unified Communications.” Each plan offers features relevant to that specific use case. For example, call monitoring would come with Contact Center and video would come with Unified Communications. This can make it easier and more cost-effective to build a phone system tailored to your needs, unlike OnSIP.


If you want to preview what 8×8 will cost, you’re out of luck. 8×8 doesn’t publicly list its rates. You’ll have to reach out to sales to get a quote — not ideal when comparing prices and features.


Also, past customers say 8×8 has a steep learning curve and involves plenty of setup. This might be impractical for small businesses that just want to get up and running quickly.


### Key features of 8×8


**


- High-volume messaging
- Contact center analytics
- AI-enabled self-service
- Omnichannel routine


### 8×8 pricing


**


At the time of this writing,[8×8 pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/8x8-pricing/) isn’t publicly available. You’ll have to contact the sales team for a customized quote.


### **7. Vonage: Best alternative for video conferencing**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calls to the US and Canada
- Video calling, with an upgrade


#### Cons


- Team messaging requires an upgrade
- Integrations require the premium plan
- No call transcription


[Vonage](https://www.quo.com/blog/vonage-alternatives/) is a legacy business phone service that’s been around since 2001. Its primary audience is mid-sized and enterprise businesses that want a unified communications platform.


Vonage’s base plan has fairly basic features: unlimited calling and texting, call analytics, and free porting. You’ll have to upgrade to a better plan to access more useful features, which include:


- Video conferencing
- Team messaging
- On-demand call recording


You should know that the cost of Vonage’s plans changes depending on the number of users. The more users you have, the less you pay per user. This puts smaller teams at a disadvantage, since you’ll have to pay more for the same service.


### Key features of Vonage


**


- SMS and MMS
- Unlimited domestic calling
- Video conferencing requires an upgrade
- Free call porting
- Free voicemail and voicemail-to-email
- Mobile and desktop apps


### Vonage pricing


**


Here’s what[Vonage pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/vonage-pricing/) is for a team of four or fewer users:


- **Mobile:** $13.99 per user per month for unlimited domestic calling, SMS/MMS, basic voicemail, and access to the desktop and mobile apps
- **Premium:** $20.99 per user per month for access to integrations, support for VoIP desk phones, video meetings with up to 200 participants, and CRM integrations
- **Advanced:** $27.99 per user per month for call groups, visual voicemail, voicemail transcription, and 15 hours of on-demand call recording


### **9. Aircall: Best for outbound sales teams needing a power dialer**


#### Pros


- Power dialer with CRM integration
- Unlimited calling in the US and Canada
- Can buy international numbers in 100+ countries


#### Cons


- Base plan has a three-user minimum
- Limited texting features
- Fewer collaboration features


[Aircall](https://www.quo.com/blog/aircall-alternatives/) is a business phone system for teams that require a power dialer. Aircall’s power dialer can be paired with a CRM to log calls for outbound sales teams that make a large number of calls each day. It also automatically identifies phone numbers on your prospect’s website, adds them to your calling queue, and syncs them with the contact in your CRM. The power dialer isn’t available on the base plan, though; you need to upgrade to at least the Professional tier.


Unlike OnSIP, Aircall offers unlimited inbound and outbound domestic calls on the base plan. You get a shared inbox to receive and answer communications as a team. Plus, with features like IVR and call recording, you won’t have to purchase more add-ons for basic features.


The drawback? Minimum users on every plan. Even Aircall’s base plan requires a three-person minimum and only allows a maximum of three teams. And the base plan only keeps call recordings for a maximum of one year — but only if you request that beyond its standard six months.


### Key features of Aircall


**


- Power dialer
- Softphone for desktop, Android, and iOS
- Time and date-based routing
- Call from any number
- Voicemail and call transcription


### Aircall pricing


**


You can choose from three different[Aircall pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/aircall-pricing/) plans:


- **Essentials:** $30 per user per month for 250+ integrations, including Slack and HubSpot, unlimited domestic calling, and shared contacts; requires a three-user minimum
- **Professional:** $50 per user per month for unlimited call recording storage, unlimited teams, smart routing, and voicemail drop; requires a three-user minimum
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing for AI developer support, custom onboarding, and unlimited outbound international calls; requires a 25-user minimum


### **10. Phone.com: Best alternative for HIPAA-compliant video calling**


#### Pros


- Unlimited calling for all plans
- Base plan is HIPAA compliant


#### Cons


- SMS requires an upgrade
- Voicemail transcriptions require an upgrade
- Call recording requires an upgrade


[Phone.com](http://quo.com/blog/phone-com-alternatives) is a user-friendly business phone system that’s HIPAA compliant on the base plan. Businesses can get unlimited calling for the US and Canada, HD video meetings, and meeting recordings. It also has free porting and no setup fees.


Keep in mind the base plan doesn’t offer SMS messaging. But upgrading to the next tier gives you unlimited texts from your business number and a shared SMS inbox. If you’re a texting-centric business, this could force you to upgrade before you’re ready.


You should also know Phone.com has fairly low ratings on G2 — currently 3.5 out of 5 stars. Past users’ most frequent complaint? That customer support isn’t always helpful.


Here’s what one reviewer had to say:


*“The back office is overseas and unintelligent, not useful for any form of problems. Working with any international call center makes companies fail and doesn’t help the customers they offer their service to. The initial setup was difficult, as I had to work with an incompetent back-office employee who couldn’t understand English or comprehend how to do their job setting me up.”* —[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/phone-com/reviews/phone-com-review-11464844)


### Key features of Phone.com


**


- Unlimited calls to the US and Canada
- SMS with an upgrade
- Custom phone number
- Smart call routing
- HD video meetings


### Phone.com pricing


**


Phone.com has three pricing plans:


- **Basic:** $15 per user per month for unlimited minutes within Canada and the US, video recording, and HIPAA-compliant calls
- **Plus: $** 22.50 per user per month for outbound SMS, voicemail transcriptions, and shared SMS inbox
- **Pro:** $33.33 per user per month for call recording, CRM integrations, and data retention for 10 years.


##


**Why businesses move to OnSIP alternatives**


OnSIP is a hosted VoIP solution that offers all the basics you need to get started with a business phone. Upgraded plans come with unlimited calls to the US and Canada, texting support, auto-attendants, and voicemail.


You can also set up a SIP trunking solution, which lets you use an on-premises PBX system to make and receive calls from traditional phone lines. It uses a unique protocol to avoid call quality and reliability issues from traditional SIP trunking.


But OnSIP isn’t a fit for most small and growing businesses, and if you look at[OnSIP pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/onsip-pricing) , you’ll see why. The Basic plan starts at $49.95 per account per month and offers pay-as-you-go rates for calling and messaging. There are usage limits for features like voicemail, ring groups, and the dial-by-name directory. To get unlimited access to these features, you’ll need to purchase the Unlimited plan at $18.95 per user. But keep in mind there’s a five-user minimum, so you’re *actually* spending $94.75 per month.


Unfortunately, this is just the tip of the iceberg.


OnSIP has several other drawbacks you should know:


### **No free trial**


OnSIP doesn’t have a free trial. That means you can’t test it out before signing up.


### **Pay-as-you-go rates for calls and messages**


On the Basic[OnSIP plan](https://www.quo.com/blog/onsip-pricing) , you’re charged for calls and messages on a per-use basis. Calls cost $0.032 per minute, and outbound SMS and MMS cost $0.01 each.


This may be fine for low-volume teams, but busy and growing companies may struggle to control costs.


Luckily, other VoIP systems like Quo offer unlimited calling and messaging in the US and Canada on *every* plan.


### **Add-ons can stack up**


OnSIP’s base plan places limits on certain key features, like five voicemail boxes per account and three ring groups. You’ll also need paid add-ons for many other features. This includes:


- **Call parking lots:** $14.95 per month for 15 channels
- **Auto-attendant, or IVR menu:** One-time $19.95 fee
- **Busy lamp field:** One-time $19.95 fee
- **Call recording:** $4.95 per user per month


These can significantly increase your spend on what’s *supposed* to be a low-cost solution.


The good news is, OnSIP isn’t the only business phone provider. Quo offers many of OnSIP’s add-ons as basic features on its base plan.


### **Working together as a team is difficult**


If team collaboration is important to you, OnSIP probably shouldn’t be your first choice


It lacks features such as:


- Conversation-related task management
- Shared contacts
- Contact notes


Without these, it could be much harder to share information or coordinate efforts to resolve customer issues.


### **Few time-saving features**


Want features to help save your team time? Or improve productivity? There aren’t many to choose from with OnSIP.


Features like voicemail transcription require subscribing to a third-party service like Phonewire. Others, like call summaries and scheduled texting, aren’t even an upgrade option. If you want more automation features like auto-replies, for example, you’re better off looking for an OnSIP alternative.


### **Not many integrations**


Unlike many other VoIP services, OnSIP doesn’t offer many integrations. You get Zendesk, Odoo, HubSpot, and a couple others for OnSIP’s trunking features. Other connectors, like Twilio, can help you turn third-party phone numbers into extensions for your team.


But apart from that, there’s not much you can do to expand OnSIP’s capabilities. You should look elsewhere if you need additional integrations for your company.


##


**Try out the best OnSIP alternative for free**


OnSIP *could* make sense for your business if you’re looking for SIP trunking or if you already have existing phone hardware and want to squeeze out the last bit of mileage. But if you’re a fast-growing team with a budget to keep, OnSIP may not be the best option on the market.


But for 90,000+ businesses, Quo is *the* next-generation phone system that can help you engage with customers, collaborate with your team, and scale with AI, without losing the personal touch.


Get unlimited calling and messaging on every plan. No need to upgrade for basic features like call recording and voicemail boxes. You’ll also have access to team collaboration tools like shared numbers, threads and mentions, and assigned tasks.


No need to take our word for it, though.


Experience it for yourself with a[seven-day free trial of Quo](https://my.quo.com/signup) .
